body: Orchestrator adversarial review of PR #268 head a1c69c4e (dotfiles-T81, CompactionDB Codex ingest and bounded ledger): normalize.py maps a Codex notify agent-turn-complete payload onto the Stop hook shape (thread-id -> session_id, client -> agent_id when present, last-assistant-message -> last_assistant_message) with a uuid5 event_uuid from thread-id + turn-id so repeated deliveries dedup; storage.py gains enforce_size_cap (oldest events in batches of 100 while in-use pages exceed capture.max_db_bytes, default 512 MiB; unpromoted candidates of capped events and already-orphaned candidates go first; durable memories and promoted candidates never; FTS index merged before the first size check and after every batch so dead segment pages never count as in use; revise round 1 after the task-level audit reproduced over-deletion, a skipped VACUUM and a skipped optimize) and vacuum_if_fragmented (forced whenever retention or the cap deleted rows or the file is still over the cap, else the 64 MiB free-page threshold), both only from the explicit prune CLI, which runs retention + cap in one transaction and VACUUMs outside it; the SessionEnd hook path is unchanged. config.py validates the new key; vendor CHANGELOG 2.0.0+dotfiles.7, MANIFEST.sha256 regenerated by a new make manifest target (proved byte-identical on origin/main), manifest pin bumped, project copy refreshed with install.py (four runtime files; hooks already identical) and a validator parity check added. Vendor suite 86 OK via make -C vendor/compactiondb test (the task's discover command fails at import on origin/main as well), 791 unit tests, render-check and validate-agent-assets ok, live check turn_stop|t1 and prune rc 0. Four Codex P2 threads fixed (f9f4b916, 8c8cf691 x3; the retention-path candidate behaviour is kept by design and bounded by the cap) and resolved by the orchestrator; no Bot review on the final head within the window; CI 13/13 green. Deviations accepted: tests/unit/test_asset_manifest.py version literals; install.py reorders .claude/settings.json (forbidden file) and was restored, recorded as a vendor follow-up.
